title: Debug: Delay Line
constraints: Intended behavior: a 4-stage delay line. On each rising edge, stage 1 takes `din`, stage 2 takes stage 1, and so on. `dout` = stage 4 (so `din` appears on `dout` exactly 4 edges later).
The starter code has **1 bug**, a classic one. The Verilog and VHDL versions show different symptoms of the same mistake.
hints: Submit the starter and check `taps`: how many distinct stages do you actually see?
Verilog: what's the difference between `=` and `<=` inside `always @(posedge clk)`?
VHDL: a *variable* updates immediately, a *signal* only at the end of the process. What does that mean for the order of the assignments?

examples.title: delay
examples.expected: dout = 11 four edges after it entered

examples.title: random
examples.expected: every stage holds a different sample
